archetype.name: Cup Contender (offense-first)
archetype.definition: The defending top team on the site, built around an elite top line and the league's best puck-moving defense, good enough to win most nights on chances alone. The open question is whether its goaltending can carry its share.

report.headline: Elite offense, shaky crease: a contender scoring through a goaltending dip
report.take:
Colorado opened last season's run as the site's No. 1 team, a 55-16-11 club that led the league in both goals for and goals against. Six games into 2026-27 the attack looks the same. The Avalanche are first in offense with 4.83 goals a game, a 55.8 xGF % that ranks 6th, and a Goal Diff / GP second only to one team. The top of the roster is carrying it. Nathan MacKinnon has 12 points on 25 shots, Martin Necas is controlling 65.6% of the expected goals when he's out there, and Cale Makar and Devon Toews both sit inside the top six on the defense tab. The forward group grades A- and the blueline grades A.

What separates this start from last season is the crease. Last year's goalies saved 34.3 goals above expected, the engine behind that No. 1 defense. This year the group is at -3.9, 26th in the league, and Mackenzie Blackwood has an .879 save percentage through five starts. That is why a team out-chancing opponents this comfortably ranks 22nd in goals against and carries a D+ goaltending grade. It also explains the 6-3 home loss to Toronto.

The numbers hide some regression in both directions. A 107.1 PDO next to below-average goaltending means 5-on-5 shooting is running very hot. Artturi Lehkonen has 4 goals on 8 shots, and an 8-4 opener padded the totals. The scoring will come down. On the other side, Colorado is one point under what its goal differential implies, and Blackwood's start is far below anything in this team's recent history. The goals against should improve as the goals for cool.

The sustainable core is the shot share and the top-end talent, and both point toward a top-five team rather than the 11th-place one the site shows today. The shape of the season depends on whether Blackwood settles. If he does, this looks like last year's team again. If he doesn't, it is a high-event club that wins plenty of regular-season games but is harder to trust in spring.

strengths.title: MacKinnon-led top-end scoring
strengths.body: MacKinnon is producing at a two-points-a-game clip, with the shot volume to back it. Necas and Lehkonen give the top six real finish, and the power play ranks 7th. Some of this is hot shooting, but the underlying chance creation is elite and should keep the offense near the top of the league.

strengths.title: A blueline that drives play
strengths.body: Makar and Toews are both top-six defensemen on the site, and the group grades A. Toews is on the ice for 62.3% of the expected goals. Puck movement from the back end is a big part of why Colorado owns the 5-on-5 chance share, and it has held up across seasons.

strengths.title: Winning the chance battle
strengths.body: A 55.8 xGF % ranks 6th and fits this team's history: it has been above 52% in each of the last five seasons. This is a repeatable edge, not a hot week.

concerns.title: Blackwood's start in the crease
concerns.body: An .879 save percentage and -3.5 GSAx in five starts are the main reason the goals against rank 22nd. Last season's elite goaltending was the foundation of the league's best defense, so this is the single biggest gap from last year's team. Five starts is a small sample, and some recovery is likely, but it is the swing factor.

concerns.title: 5-on-5 shooting is unsustainably hot
concerns.body: A 107.1 PDO with negative goaltending means the shooting side is doing all the lifting. Lehkonen's 4 goals on 8 shots is the clearest example. Expect the goals-per-game figure to fall from its current pace even if the chances keep coming.

concerns.title: Depth scoring and coverage leaks
concerns.body: Kadri has no goals on 18 shots and T.J. Hughes none on 15, so the middle six leans on the top line. In their own end, opponents' defensemen are getting more than their usual production against Colorado. The depth shooters should start finishing more, while the coverage lapses are worth watching.

trend.note: Colorado has not won more than two in a row or lost more than one, alternating results through October while out-chancing nearly everyone. Six games is too few to call a direction beyond a strong, if leaky, baseline.

weekAhead.headline: Two home games, then the league's worst team and a leaky Devils
weekAhead.body:
The week opens at home with a rematch against Dallas, a night after Colorado won 3-2 in Dallas. The Stars have the league's best goals-against and A+ goaltending, but they rank 30th in offense. Expect a low-scoring test of whether Colorado's top line can crack a defense that has held centers furthest under their norms. Pittsburgh follows at home; it is a middle-of-the-pack side that gives up more than expected to wingers.

The road swing is the softer half. Philadelphia is 0-5-3, last on the site, and gets out-chanced worse than anyone. New Jersey arrives the next night on a back-to-back. The Devils lead the league in both 5-on-5 shares, but they pair that with D+ goaltending and a 27th-ranked penalty kill. They also rank last in points allowed to both centers and defensemen, which sets up well for MacKinnon, Necas, Makar and Toews. A 3-1 week is a reasonable expectation.

keyMatchups.title: MacKinnon line vs Dallas's wall
keyMatchups.body: Dallas ranks 1st in holding centers under their expected points and has saved 6.4 goals above expected. Colorado's center-heavy top six will find goals scarce here. This is the one game where the hot shooting is most likely to cool.

keyMatchups.title: Colorado power play vs Devils PK
keyMatchups.body: Colorado's power play runs at 23.8%, 7th in the league, against a New Jersey kill at 70.6%, 27th. The Devils also allow the most points to defensemen of any team, which suits Makar and Toews.

keyMatchups.title: Philadelphia's possession collapse
keyMatchups.body: The Flyers own 34.5% of the expected goals and 40% of the shot attempts at 5-on-5, both last in the league, with F grades up front and on the blueline. This is the clearest win on the schedule.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Blackwood starts both ends of the Philadelphia–New Jersey back-to-back, and his save percentage across the week.

restOfSeason.body:
The chance share and the top-end talent are real and match a five-season track record. A team out-chancing opponents at this rate should finish near the top of the Central and well inside the playoff field. The scoring pace will cool as the 107.1 PDO comes back to earth, so expect more like a strong offense than a historic one.

The defensive numbers should move the other way. Last season's goaltending was elite, and even a return to average from Blackwood would cut the goals against meaningfully. The ceiling depends on whether the crease gets to average or back toward last year's level. The floor is still a playoff team because the skaters drive play.
swingFactors: Blackwood's save percentage settling to league average or better
Depth centers like Kadri starting to finish

confidence.note: Only six games and five Blackwood starts, but the shot share matches years of history.
